verses.en: But Job answered and said,
verses.pt: Então Jó, respondendo, disse:
verses.en_web: Then Job answered,
verses.en_bbe: And Job made answer and said,

verses.en: O that my grief were throughly weighed, and my calamity laid in the balances together!
verses.pt: Oxalá de fato se pesasse a minhá magoa, e juntamente na balança se pusesse a minha calamidade!
verses.en_web: “Oh that my anguish were weighed, and all my calamity laid in the balances!
verses.en_bbe: If only my passion might be measured, and put into the scales against my trouble!

verses.en: For now it would be heavier than the sand of the sea: therefore my words are swallowed up.
verses.pt: Pois, na verdade, seria mais pesada do que a areia dos mares; por isso é que as minhas palavras têm sido temerárias.
verses.en_web: For now it would be heavier than the sand of the seas, therefore have my words been rash.
verses.en_bbe: For then its weight would be more than the sand of the seas: because of this my words have been uncontrolled.

verses.en: For the arrows of the Almighty are within me, the poison whereof drinketh up my spirit: the terrors of God do set themselves in array against me.
verses.pt: Porque as flechas do Todo-Poderoso se cravaram em mim, e o meu espírito suga o veneno delas; os terrores de Deus se arregimentam contra mim.
verses.en_web: For the arrows of the Almighty are within me. My spirit drinks up their poison. The terrors of God set themselves in array against me.
verses.en_bbe: For the arrows of the Ruler of all are present with me, and their poison goes deep into my spirit: his army of fears is put in order against me.

verses.en: Doth the wild ass bray when he hath grass? or loweth the ox over his fodder?
verses.pt: Zurrará o asno montês quando tiver erva? Ou mugirá o boi junto ao seu pasto?:
verses.en_web: Does the wild donkey bray when he has grass? Or does the ox low over his fodder?
verses.en_bbe: Does the ass of the fields give out his voice when he has grass? or does the ox make sounds over his food?

verses.en: Can that which is unsavoury be eaten without salt? or is there any taste in the white of an egg?
verses.pt: Pode se comer sem sal o que é insípido? Ou há gosto na clara do ovo?
verses.en_web: Can that which has no flavor be eaten without salt? Or is there any taste in the white of an egg?
verses.en_bbe: Will a man take food which has no taste without salt? or is there any taste in the soft substance of purslain?

verses.en: The things that my soul refused to touch are as my sorrowful meat.
verses.pt: Nessas coisas a minha alma recusa tocar, pois são para mim qual comida repugnante.
verses.en_web: My soul refuses to touch them. They are as loathsome food to me.
verses.en_bbe: My soul has no desire for such things, they are as disease in my food.

verses.en: Oh that I might have my request; and that God would grant me the thing that I long for!
verses.pt: Quem dera que se cumprisse o meu rogo, e que Deus me desse o que anelo!
verses.en_web: “Oh that I might have my request, that God would grant the thing that I long for,
verses.en_bbe: If only I might have an answer to my prayer, and God would give me my desire!

verses.en: Even that it would please God to destroy me; that he would let loose his hand, and cut me off!
verses.pt: que fosse do agrado de Deus esmagar-me; que soltasse a sua mão, e me exterminasse!
verses.en_web: even that it would please God to crush me; that he would let loose his hand, and cut me off!
verses.en_bbe: If only he would be pleased to put an end to me; and would let loose his hand, so that I might be cut off!

verses.en: Then should I yet have comfort; yea, I would harden myself in sorrow: let him not spare; for I have not concealed the words of the Holy One.
verses.pt: Isto ainda seria a minha consolação, e exultaria na dor que não me poupa; porque não tenho negado as palavras do Santo.
verses.en_web: Be it still my consolation, yes, let me exult in pain that doesn’t spare, that I have not denied the words of the Holy One.
verses.en_bbe: So I would still have comfort, and I would have joy in the pains of death, for I have not been false to the words of the Holy One.

verses.en: What is my strength, that I should hope? and what is mine end, that I should prolong my life?
verses.pt: Qual é a minha força, para que eu espere? Ou qual é o meu fim, para que me porte com paciência?
verses.en_web: What is my strength, that I should wait? What is my end, that I should be patient?
verses.en_bbe: Have I strength to go on waiting, or have I any end to be looking forward to?

verses.en: Is my strength the strength of stones? or is my flesh of brass?
verses.pt: É a minha força a força da pedra? Ou é de bronze a minha carne?
verses.en_web: Is my strength the strength of stones? Or is my flesh of brass?
verses.en_bbe: Is my strength the strength of stones, or is my flesh brass?

verses.en: Is not my help in me? and is wisdom driven quite from me?
verses.pt: Na verdade não há em mim socorro nenhum. Não me desamparou todo o auxílio eficaz?
verses.en_web: Isn’t it that I have no help in me, That wisdom is driven quite from me?
verses.en_bbe: I have no help in myself, and wisdom is completely gone from me.

verses.en: To him that is afflicted pity should be shewed from his friend; but he forsaketh the fear of the Almighty.
verses.pt: Ao que desfalece devia o amigo mostrar compaixão; mesmo ao que abandona o temor do Todo-Poderoso.
verses.en_web: “To him who is ready to faint, kindness should be shown from his friend; even to him who forsakes the fear of the Almighty.
verses.en_bbe: He whose heart is shut against his friend has given up the fear of the Ruler of all.

verses.en: My brethren have dealt deceitfully as a brook, and as the stream of brooks they pass away;
verses.pt: Meus irmãos houveram-se aleivosamente, como um ribeiro, como a torrente dos ribeiros que passam,
verses.en_web: My brothers have dealt deceitfully as a brook, as the channel of brooks that pass away;
verses.en_bbe: My friends have been false like a stream, like streams in the valleys which come to an end:

verses.en: Which are blackish by reason of the ice, and wherein the snow is hid:
verses.pt: os quais se turvam com o gelo, e neles se esconde a neve;
verses.en_web: Which are black by reason of the ice, in which the snow hides itself.
verses.en_bbe: Which are dark because of the ice, and the snow falling into them;

verses.en: What time they wax warm, they vanish: when it is hot, they are consumed out of their place.
verses.pt: no tempo do calor vão minguando; e quando o calor vem, desaparecem do seu lugar.
verses.en_web: In the dry season, they vanish. When it is hot, they are consumed out of their place.
verses.en_bbe: Under the burning sun they are cut off, and come to nothing because of the heat.

verses.en: The paths of their way are turned aside; they go to nothing, and perish.
verses.pt: As caravanas se desviam do seu curso; sobem ao deserto, e perecem.
verses.en_web: The caravans that travel beside them turn away. They go up into the waste, and perish.
verses.en_bbe: The camel-trains go out of their way; they go up into the waste and come to destruction.

verses.en: The troops of Tema looked, the companies of Sheba waited for them.
verses.pt: As caravanas de Tema olham; os viandantes de Sabá por eles esperam.
verses.en_web: The caravans of Tema looked. The companies of Sheba waited for them.
verses.en_bbe: The camel-trains of Tema were searching with care, the bands of Sheba were waiting for them:

verses.en: They were confounded because they had hoped; they came thither, and were ashamed.
verses.pt: Ficam envergonhados por terem confiado; e, chegando ali, se confundem.
verses.en_web: They were distressed because they were confident. They came there, and were confounded.
verses.en_bbe: They were put to shame because of their hope; they came and their hope was gone.

verses.en: For now ye are no thing; ye see my casting down, and are afraid.
verses.pt: Agora, pois, tais vos tornastes para mim; vedes a minha calamidade e temeis.
verses.en_web: For now you are nothing. You see a terror, and are afraid.
verses.en_bbe: So have you now become to me; you see my sad condition and are in fear.

verses.en: Did I say, Bring unto me? or, Give a reward for me of your substance?
verses.pt: Acaso disse eu: Dai-me um presente? Ou: Fazei-me uma oferta de vossos bens?
verses.en_web: Did I say, ‘Give to me?’ or, ‘Offer a present for me from your substance?’
verses.en_bbe: Did I say, Give me something? or, Make a payment for me out of your wealth?

verses.en: Or, Deliver me from the enemy’s hand? or, Redeem me from the hand of the mighty?
verses.pt: Ou: Livrai-me das mãos do adversário? Ou: Resgatai-me das mãos dos opressores ?
verses.en_web: or, ‘Deliver me from the adversary’s hand?’ or, ‘Redeem me from the hand of the oppressors?’
verses.en_bbe: Or, Get me out of the power of my hater? or, Give money so that I may be free from the power of the cruel ones?

verses.en: Teach me, and I will hold my tongue: and cause me to understand wherein I have erred.
verses.pt: Ensinai-me, e eu me calarei; e fazei-me entender em que errei.
verses.en_web: “Teach me, and I will hold my peace. Cause me to understand wherein I have erred.
verses.en_bbe: Give me teaching and I will be quiet; and make me see my error.

verses.en: How forcible are right words! but what doth your arguing reprove?
verses.pt: Quão poderosas são as palavras da boa razão! Mas que é o que a vossa argüição reprova?
verses.en_web: How forcible are words of uprightness! But your reproof, what does it reprove?
verses.en_bbe: How pleasing are upright words! but what force is there in your arguments?

verses.en: Do ye imagine to reprove words, and the speeches of one that is desperate, which are as wind?
verses.pt: Acaso pretendeis reprovar palavras, embora sejam as razões do desesperado como vento?
verses.en_web: Do you intend to reprove words, since the speeches of one who is desperate are as wind?
verses.en_bbe: My words may seem wrong to you, but the words of him who has no hope are for the wind.

verses.en: Yea, ye overwhelm the fatherless, and ye dig a pit for your friend.
verses.pt: Até quereis lançar sortes sobre o órfão, e fazer mercadoria do vosso amigo.
verses.en_web: Yes, you would even cast lots for the fatherless, and make merchandise of your friend.
verses.en_bbe: Truly, you are such as would give up the child of a dead man to his creditors, and would make a profit out of your friend.

verses.en: Now therefore be content, look upon me; for it is evident unto you if I lie.
verses.pt: Agora, pois, por favor, olhai para, mim; porque de certo à vossa face não mentirei.
verses.en_web: Now therefore be pleased to look at me, for surely I shall not lie to your face.
verses.en_bbe: Now then, let your eyes be turned to me, for truly I will not say what is false to your face.

verses.en: Return, I pray you, let it not be iniquity; yea, return again, my righteousness is in it.
verses.pt: Mudai de parecer, peço-vos, não haja injustiça; sim, mudai de parecer, que a minha causa é justa.
verses.en_web: Please return. Let there be no injustice. Yes, return again. My cause is righteous.
verses.en_bbe: Let your minds be changed, and do not have an evil opinion of me; yes, be changed, for my righteousness is still in me.

verses.en: Is there iniquity in my tongue? cannot my taste discern perverse things?
verses.pt: Há iniqüidade na minha língua? Ou não poderia o meu paladar discernir coisas perversas?
verses.en_web: Is there injustice on my tongue? Can’t my taste discern mischievous things?
verses.en_bbe: Is there evil in my tongue? is not the cause of my trouble clear to me?
